newsitem.title: CHILE: Escondida copper workers end strike vote.
newsitem.headline: Escondida copper workers end strike vote.

text.p: Striking workers at Chile's Escondida copper mine ended voting at 2000 local/0000 GMT Wednesday on whether to accept the firm's latest pay offer, a union official said.
"They've opened the urns and they've begun counting," Pablo Godoy of the Chilean Mining Confederation told Reuters by telephone.
The mine's 350-odd unionized workers stopped work Friday to demand progress in wage negotiations. The rest of the mine's 2,000-strong workforce did not join the strike.
Mine CEO Ken Pickering said Wednesday that the strike had slown down operations slightly but that output and shipments of both concentrates and cathodes was normal.
The 800,000-tonne-a-year mine is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd and RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd.
BHP owns 57.5 percent of Escondidia, RTZ-CRA owns 30 percent, the Japanese owned consortium JECO holds 10 percent and International Finance Corp 2.5 percent.
